data.about: The side span of Tower Bridge: a chain hung from the short abutment tower F and the tall main tower I, forced through the anchor point E — a three-point funicular problem. The deck weight, a one-sided live load on either span, and a moving point load Q each re-pose the same problem: trial funiculars give division points on the load line, parallels to the chords F–E and E–I give the pole, and the chain re-forms — swinging between the two live-load extremes.

steps.caption: step through with the slider, press play, or use ←/→
steps.title: How to draw this scheme

steps.caption: left: the chain hangs from the short tower F and the tall tower I, and is anchored at E on hanger 6 (drag F, E, I!) — 15 hangers carry the deck
steps.title: The side span of Tower Bridge

steps.caption: left: each hanger carries one strip of the green deck band, split at E’s hanger — right: 15 equal loads stacked on the load line (top = rightmost strip)
steps.title: The deck load g

steps.caption: both sides at once: the whole deck weighs R_g — on its centroid line in the form diagram AND as the full load line
steps.title: The resultant R_g

steps.caption: the split at E’s hanger: left band = 5.5 strips (R₁), right = 9.5 strips (R₂) — right: the load line divides at the same ratio
steps.title: R₁ and R₂

steps.caption: right: any pole o′₁ with rays to the right-span loads — left: a trial funicular between E’s and I’s verticals, drawn in the workspace above
steps.title: Trial pole o′₁ — right span

steps.caption: right: a second pole o′₂ for the left-span loads — left: its trial funicular between E’s and F’s verticals
steps.title: Trial pole o′₂ — left span

steps.caption: left: close each trial (dashed) — right: parallels through o′₁ and o′₂ cut the load line at the division points i₁ and i₂ (they do not depend on the trial!)
steps.title: Closing lines → division points

steps.caption: left: the chords F–E and E–I (orange dashed) — right: through i₁ ∥ E–I and through i₂ ∥ F–E: the pole o, with rays to the load line
steps.title: Chords → the pole o

steps.caption: left: from F, one side parallel to each ray — through E, onto I, and over the saddle to the backstay (dash-dotted: the dead-load chain)
steps.title: The chain under g

steps.caption: right: the polygon closes — A = from the bottom of the load line to o, B = from o back to the top — left: the chain pulls at F and over the saddle at I
steps.title: Reactions A and B

steps.caption: replace each span’s load by its resultant: two strings per span through F, E, I lie ON the chord lines (orange dashed) — right: the sub-poles recombine into o
steps.title: Check: superposition

steps.caption: left: the left band is loaded to factor_q·g (orange) — right: its load line: R₂ = R_g unchanged, R₁ = R_g + R_q₁ grows
steps.title: Live load q₁ on the left span

steps.caption: right: the SAME division-point construction on the new load line (parallels to the chords) gives the pole o₁ and its fan
steps.title: The pole o₁

steps.caption: left: the chain re-forms — still through F, E, I, but sagging deeper on the loaded left span; reactions A, B
steps.title: The chain under g + q₁

steps.caption: left: now the right band is loaded (orange) — right: its load line: R₂ = R_g + R_q₂ grows, R₁ = R_g stays
steps.title: Live load q₂ on the right span

steps.caption: right: division points + chord parallels once more → pole o₂ with its fan of rays
steps.title: The pole o₂

steps.caption: left: the chain swings the other way — deeper on the right span; reactions A, B
steps.title: The chain under g + q₂

steps.caption: the chain always passes through F, E and I, but one-sided live load swings it between these two extremes around the dead-load shape
steps.title: The envelope

steps.caption: left: a wagon load Q = factor_Q·strip on hanger positionQ (drag it along the deck!) — right: Q on its own small load line
steps.title: A point load Q

steps.caption: left: alone, Q would hang as a triangle through F, E, I — its kink S on the chord lines extended (dashed) — right: the parallels give Q’s own little pole triangle
steps.title: Q alone: the chord lines

steps.caption: right: the full load line again, with Q widening its strip’s gap (orange, like the original) — left: Q stays on its hanger
steps.title: Q joins the load line

steps.caption: right: a trial pole o′₁ with rays to the right-span loads (now including Q if it is there) — left: the trial funicular above the chain
steps.title: Trial pole o′₁ again

steps.caption: right: the second trial pole o′₂ for the left-span loads — left: its trial funicular
steps.title: Trial pole o′₂ again

steps.caption: left: the dashed closings — and the span resultants’ lines of action — right: parallels through o′₁ / o′₂ cut the load line at i₁ and i₂
steps.title: Closings → i₁ and i₂

steps.caption: right: through i₁ ∥ E–I and through i₂ ∥ F–E: the pole o₃ of the full load, with its fan
steps.title: The pole o₃

steps.caption: left: THE chain — through F, E and I, kinked under Q, over the saddle into the backstay anchor
steps.title: The chain under g + Q

steps.caption: right: A = from below the load line to o₃, B = from o₃ back to the top — left: the chain pulls at the abutment F and along the backstay at I
steps.title: Reactions

steps.caption: the trials step back; the chain resolves pink = tension (pipes ∝ force). Drag Q along the deck, drag E, F, I or the poles; play with the sliders
steps.title: Pure tension
